claim_text: An employee took the data, the company says
summary: Premise Health says an employee violated its security policies and misappropriated company data, starting on or about March 26, 2026.
detail: The company has not named the employee, given their role or said why they took it. We do not name them.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company's website notice and its notice letter both say an employee misappropriated the data.

claim_text: Premise Health says it was not a hacking or ransomware event
summary: Premise Health's website notice says: 'This was not a hacking or ransomware event.' This is the company's own statement.
detail: Its notice letters and state filings describe an employee taking the data, which fits that account, but no independent investigation has been published to confirm there was no outside intrusion. We found no claim by any hacker or ransomware group.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company's own notice says it in these words; the label confirms that Premise Health said it, not that it has been independently checked.

claim_text: Why the employee took the data, and what was done with it
summary: Premise Health has not said why the employee copied the data or where it went.
detail: ISMG reports the company did not answer questions about the employee's role or how the activity was found.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No source gives a motive or says what happened to the data afterwards.

claim_text: The employee was fired and the case reported to police
summary: Premise Health says the employee has been terminated and the incident reported to law enforcement.
detail: No charges or law-enforcement statement have been made public that we found.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Both the website notice and the letter say so.

claim_text: Premise Health found it on Sept 18, 2026
summary: Premise Health says it discovered the employee's actions on Sept 18, 2026, and at once revoked the employee's credentials and system access.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The notice and the letter give the discovery date and the response.

claim_text: The taking began on or about March 26, 2026
summary: Premise Health says the employee misappropriated data beginning on or about March 26, 2026.
detail: The company gives a start date but no end date.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The notice and the letter give the start date.

claim_text: Oregon's listing gives breach dates of March 26 to 30, 2026
summary: The Oregon Department of Justice's breach list shows Premise Health's breach dates as March 26 to March 30, 2026.
detail: The company's own notice gives only a start date, so this is the only public end date. It has not been explained.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The state's listing of the company's filing shows these dates.

claim_text: A first analysis of the data came on Oct 14
summary: Premise Health says it received a preliminary analysis of the relevant data on Oct 14, 2026, then validated it before notifying people.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The notice and the letter give the date.

claim_text: Notice letters went out from Nov 6, 2026
summary: Premise Health's sample letter is dated Nov 6, 2026, and the Oregon and Washington listings record notices from that date.
detail: Some letters went to parents of minors whose data was involved, per the letter.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The dated letter and the two state listings agree on Nov 6.

summary: Premise Health's filing listed by Oregon gives 2,760,238 people affected in total.
detail: Earlier counts summed from a few states were far lower: 416,700 in five states by Nov 11, per The HIPAA Journal.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The Oregon listing shows the number affected the company reported.

claim_text: Texas, South Carolina, Washington, Massachusetts and Vermont counts
summary: State filings list 261,654 people in Texas, 60,641 in South Carolina, 49,444 in Washington, 43,046 in Massachusetts and 1,948 in Vermont.
detail: We read Washington's listing ourselves; the other four counts come from two outlets that read the state postings.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Washington's listing shows 49,444; both outlets report the same five counts.

claim_text: Names, birth dates, Social Security numbers, insurance and treatment information
summary: Premise Health says the data varied by person and may include name, address, date of birth, Social Security or other government ID number, health insurance and diagnostic or treatment information.
detail: Also other information given in connection with eligibility for services.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The notice and the letter list these data types.

claim_text: Premise Health says it is not aware of any misuse
summary: Premise Health says it is not aware of any misuse of the personal information.
detail: Not being aware of misuse is not proof there was none.
label: Confirmed

summary: Premise Health is offering free Experian IdentityWorks credit monitoring; the enrolment details are in each person's letter.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The letter names the service; the website notice points to the letter.

summary: Premise Health says there was no interruption to its operations and its sites remain open to patients.
label: Confirmed

claim_text: Premise Health serves about 11 million members in 46 states
summary: Premise Health runs employer-sponsored health centers and serves about 11 million members in 46 states, two outlets report.
detail: The HIPAA Journal also cites more than 800 wellness centers.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Two independent outlets give the same figures.

claim_text: At least 11 lawsuits have been filed against Premise Health
summary: Federal court dockets in Nashville (Middle District of Tennessee) show at least 11 cases against Premise Health Holding Corp. filed between Nov 11 and Nov 19, 2026, at least one as a proposed class action.
detail: The dockets list complaints, summonses and scheduling orders. We have read one complaint (see the claim on the lawsuit that alleges a hack); the others are not yet in the public archive. A lawsuit is a claim, not a finding; no court has ruled. We do not name the people suing.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The court dockets list each case, its filing date and Premise Health as defendant.
notes: Counted: 10 cases on the CourtListener results page (Nov 13-19) plus case 3:26-cv-01819 (Nov 11) on Justia. A further Nov 13 case appears on Justia but was not counted.

claim_text: One lawsuit alleges Premise Health was hacked by outside criminals
summary: A proposed class action filed Nov 13 (case 3:26-cv-01843) says the company 'was hacked' and that 'cybercriminals infiltrated' its systems, some of it stated 'on information and belief'.
detail: The complaint's only cited source for what happened is Premise Health's own notice, which says this was 'not a hacking or ransomware event', and the complaint also quotes the company's statement that an employee misappropriated the data. It offers no evidence of an outside intruder. A complaint is one side's allegations; no court has ruled.
label: Unverified
why_it_supports: The complaint text (pages 2, 4 and 8) makes these allegations and cites only the company notice and state breach filings for the facts.
notes: Read the 44-page complaint PDF from RECAP. Wording looks like standard data-breach complaint language. Plaintiff not named on the page per privacy rule.
